## 2.3.3 - 2026-11-02

### Fixes

- **Cross-model continuations no longer fail with `400 missing messages[N].reasoning_content`** ([#334](https://github.com/rashidrazak/opencode-cmd-provider/issues/334), [#337](https://github.com/rashidrazak/opencode-cmd-provider/pull/337)): when a session started on a non-reasoning model continues on a reasoning model, earlier assistant turns have no reasoning to replay. The plugin now sends the placeholder `(no reasoning recorded for this earlier turn)` for every such turn — text-only and tool-bearing — on both the legacy `/alpha/generate` transport and the Provider API OpenAI-compatible path. Requests for non-reasoning models are unchanged.

## 2.3.2 - 2026-10-30

**Fixes — HTTP failures now say which URL the request reached and which
credential it used.** A base URL that already ended in `/provider/v1` produced
an unexplained `404`, and a `401` from a stale CLI login looked exactly like a
bad key. Every HTTP failure now prints `(POST <url>)`, and a `401` adds the
credential's display-only source — never the key.

### Fixes

- **The request URL in every HTTP error, and the ignored CLI variable in the
  missing-key error**
  ([#326](https://github.com/rashidrazak/opencode-cmd-provider/issues/326),
  [#328](https://github.com/rashidrazak/opencode-cmd-provider/pull/328)): every
  HTTP failure now ends with `(POST <url>)`, with userinfo stripped so a proxy
  URL that embeds a credential cannot leak it through the message. A `404` from
  a `baseURL` that already ends in `/provider/v1` is now self-explanatory. When
  no key resolves and `COMMAND_CODE_API_KEY` is set, the missing-key error
  names it and says this plugin reads `COMMANDCODE_API_KEY`. The official
  variable is diagnosed, never read, so credential precedence is unchanged.
- **A `401` names the credential that was used**
  ([#327](https://github.com/rashidrazak/opencode-cmd-provider/issues/327),
  [#329](https://github.com/rashidrazak/opencode-cmd-provider/pull/329)): a
  `401` now appends `, credential: Host connection`,
  `, credential: COMMANDCODE_API_KEY` or `, credential: legacy file <path>`, so
  a stale `~/.commandcode/auth.json` no longer looks like a rejected key. The
  credential and its label are resolved in the same pass that builds the
  `Authorization` header, so a mid-ladder rotation cannot leave them
  disagreeing. Only a `401` names a credential — a `403` remains a plan or
  version gate — and a caller-supplied `Authorization` overlay suppresses the
  label, since the ladder no longer describes what was sent.
- **README and technical reference**: CLI-login reuse is scoped to `cmd login`
  (`~/.commandcode/auth.json`), `COMMAND_CODE_API_KEY` is documented as not
  read, `COMMANDCODE_API_BASE` is documented as the server root without
  `/provider/v1`, and troubleshooting gains rows for the double-`/provider/v1`
  `404` and a stale legacy-file `401`.

### Model catalog

- Refreshed to `command-code@1.88.2`; membership, costs, modalities,
  classification and deals are unchanged from 2.3.1 — only the refresh stamps
  moved.
- The models-page slug map is re-pinned: five pins whose Snapshot ids no longer
  ship are pruned, and sixteen shipped models the live models page now carries
  are pinned (`gpt-6.1-sol`, `gpt-6.1-terra`, `claude-sonnet-5-5`,
  `claude-haiku-5-5`, `kimi-k3-1-pro`, `mistral-large-4`, …). `jev/jev-1-14-0`
  stays unpinned until the catalog ships them.

## 2.3.1 - 2026-10-28

**Fixes — every Command Code model shows `[CMD]` on OpenCode v2, and Beam
works on the Go plan.**

### Fixes

- **`[CMD]` on every model in the v2 picker**
  ([#321](https://github.com/rashidrazak/opencode-cmd-provider/pull/321)):
  models.dev now lists a `commandcode` provider, and OpenCode v2 adds its
  models before the plugin runs. The plugin took those for user
  declarations and left them alone, so 71 of 94 models kept models.dev's
  names, limits, cost and modalities and showed without `[CMD]`. Every
  Snapshot model now takes the plugin's entry. User config is applied after
  plugins, so your own model names and settings still win, and routing is
  unchanged. v1 was not affected.
- **Reasoning replayed on the Go-plan wire**
  ([#322](https://github.com/rashidrazak/opencode-cmd-provider/pull/322)):
  the legacy `/alpha/generate` transport dropped earlier assistant
  reasoning, and Beam 1.0 answers HTTP 400 for a turn when any earlier
  assistant message omits it. Reasoning models now replay it as a
  `{ type: "reasoning", text }` content part, the shape the official
  command-code client sends. This applies to every reasoning model on the Go
  plan, so those requests now carry earlier reasoning as input. Provider API
  requests (GOAT and above) are unchanged.
- **The repo's dev plugin no longer shadows the installed one**
  ([#320](https://github.com/rashidrazak/opencode-cmd-provider/pull/320)):
  the working-tree entry moved from `.opencode/plugins/` to
  `dev/opencode-plugin/`, so `opencode plugin check` and `update` work again
  from inside the repo. Contributors only; the published package is
  unchanged.

### Model catalog

- No changes: the live catalog, reasoning classification and deals match
  2.3.0.

## 2.3.0 - 2026-10-27

**Highlight — new models reach you without a plugin update.** The plugin now
takes its model list from the Command Code model catalog's client view
(`GET /provider/v1/models?view=client`) instead of the `command-code`
package's `models.md`, and keeps a cached copy that a background fetch
refreshes on every start
([#318](https://github.com/rashidrazak/opencode-cmd-provider/pull/318),
ADR-0024, addresses
[#140](https://github.com/rashidrazak/opencode-cmd-provider/issues/140)).
`models.md` had become a frozen rendering of that catalog, which is why
`gpt-6.1-terra` and `moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro` were live in the CLI but
missing here; both now ship. The release also lands the 2026-10-27 catalog
refresh, which follows Command Code's GOAT and Pro repricing.

### Features

- **Model list from the catalog endpoint, cached at startup**
  ([#318](https://github.com/rashidrazak/opencode-cmd-provider/pull/318)):
  every catalog record that is not `hidden` ships; hidden records are
  reported by the refresh, never shipped. Startup never waits on the
  network: it reads the cache at
  `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/opencode-cmd-provider/models.json` (~1 ms) and merges it
  over the bundled Snapshot as a union — a cached row may add or refresh a
  model, never remove one, so a stale cache cannot hide a shipped model. A
  background fetch, started from both the v1 `config` hook and the v2
  `setup()`, primes the cache for the next start. Any cache defect falls
  back to the bundled Snapshot, and a failed fetch never surfaces as an
  error. `COMMANDCODE_CATALOG_URL` overrides the endpoint;
  `COMMANDCODE_DISABLE_CATALOG_SYNC=1` turns the fetch off.

### Fixes

- **The catalog fetch runs on both hosts**: it was first started only from
  the v1 `config` hook, which a v2 host never calls, and then only from
  `setup()`, which a v1 host never calls. Each startup path now has a test
  that fails if its call is dropped.
- **The catalog fetch stays off the transport base URL**: it no longer
  derives its URL from `COMMANDCODE_API_BASE`, so a session pointed at a
  mock or a compatible proxy still refreshes the cache instead of silently
  getting a 404.
- **Exact context lengths**: 22 models' context lengths come from the
  catalog's exact value (for example `1048576`) instead of a decimal parse
  of `1.05M`.
- **The slug-map drift report always runs**: it ran before the enrichment
  ladders and silently skipped whenever no record needed the models page.

### Model catalog

- Membership 92 → 94, sourced from the catalog endpoint
  (FACTS_PACKAGE_VERSION stays `1.88.0`; it still feeds the
  `x-command-code-version` header).
- `scripts/parse-facts.mjs`, `scripts/parse-modalities.mjs`, their tests and
  `tests/fixtures/models.md` are removed. Context, costs, efforts and input
  modalities now come from the catalog record.

| Model                      | Change | Before | After                                        |
| -------------------------- | ------ | ------ | -------------------------------------------- |
| `gpt-6.1-terra`            | added  | —      | GPT-6.1 Terra · 1050000 ctx · $1 / $5 per M  |
| `moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro` | added  | —      | Kimi K3.1 Pro · 1048576 ctx · $2 / $10 per M |

### Reasoning classification

- Both new models are classified; all 94 Snapshot models are covered.

### Deals catalog

- Upstream repriced the plans: GOAT is $10/mo for up to $100 of usage
  ($20 per 5 hours, $50 weekly), was $70 ($14 / $35); Pro is $20/mo for up to
  $110 ($22 / $55), was $80 ($16 / $40).
- The docs reworded those money cells from "$70 of usage" to "Up to $100 of
  usage"; the RSC parser accepts the "Up to " qualifier, and any other
  phrasing stays a shape change.
- Deals records added for `gpt-6.1-terra` (premium, with standard and
  long-context bands) and `moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro` (open source).
- The plan-summary test derives plan figures from the generated catalogs, so
  a repricing surfaces as a refresh diff instead of a re
